s: MHCLG statutory rough-sleeping snapshot: 3,898 people sleeping rough on a single night in autumn 2024, up 20% on 2023
d: Rough sleeping in England rose to 3,898 in autumn 2024, a 20% increase year-on-year and the highest since records began. Concentrated in London and the major conurbations.

s: NHS England RTT: 7.6 million people waiting for treatment
d: The NHS waiting list stands at 7.6 million; 3.1 million have waited over 18 weeks. Cancer and mental-health waits are the fastest-growing.

s: JRF: 4.3 million children (29%) in relative poverty after housing costs, 2023/24
d: Child poverty rose to 4.3 million (29%) in 2023/24. Deep poverty (below 50% median) affects 2.6 million children. London and the North East have the highest rates.

s: Scottish Government: 24% of children in relative poverty 2023/24
d: Scotland's child poverty rate is 24%, with a statutory target to cut it to 10% by 2030. Glasgow has the lowest life expectancy in the UK.

s: Welsh Gov: 28% of children in relative poverty
d: Wales has the highest working-age poverty rate in Britain; 28% of children in poverty.

p: 1 in 4 adults with a mental-health condition
s: NHS Digital: 1 in 4 adults experience a mental-health condition; NHS talking-therapy waiting lists exceed 1 million
d: Demand for NHS mental-health services is at record high; 1.4 million people are waiting for talking therapies, with average waits over 6 weeks and rising.

s: London Councils: over 183,000 Londoners in temporary accommodation, a record high
d: London has a record 183,000 people in temporary accommodation; Newham and other East London boroughs have the highest concentrations. Driven by benefit caps and private-rent unaffordability.

s: Greater Manchester combined authority: 132,410 households in TA, highest outside London
d: Greater Manchester has 132,410 households in temporary accommodation — the highest outside London — reflecting a sharp post-pandemic rise in family homelessness.

s: Birmingham City Council: family homelessness and TA placements at multi-year high
d: Birmingham's household homelessness and temporary-accommodation use are at a multi-year high after the council's section 114 notice and housing-market pressure.

s: Campaign to End Loneliness: ~3.5 million people in England chronically lonely
d: An estimated 3.5 million people in England are chronically lonely, with the highest rates among young adults, the bereaved and those with long-term conditions.

p: Food bank use at record high
s: Trussell Trust: 3.1 million emergency food parcels distributed in 2023/24
d: Trussell Trust distributed 3.1 million emergency food parcels in 2023/24, a record, with universal-credit claimants the largest user group.
